messages:
sam: FYI - after the continuous-batching merge on canary I'm seeing steady KV cache memory growth for long-context sessions. p95 token latency up ~12% on chat-longseq. Suspect fragmentation + head-of-line blocking when batch merges
lee: Ugh. Can you paste the perf snapshot + which model/seq len?
maria: also which canary commit? any logs from runtime gc/eviction?
sam: model=rw-13b, seq ~32k for a replication test. commit=cb4d9f. attaching a small heap sample i grabbed (summarized):
```
kv_pages_total=16384
kv_pages_in_use=15760
kv_fragments=412
avg_fragment_size=38 pages
page_alloc_rate=120/s
page_eviction_rate=0.4/s
resident_rss_growth=+850MB over 20m
```
Not sure why eviction_rate is low while alloc rate is high.
lee: that screams fragmentation - lots of small fragments getting pinned by active batches. When a merged batch includes requests with overlapping KV ranges the head request can block eviction for many pages. I ran a flamegraph and saw lots of time in kv_cache:pin_pages and batch_merge:hold_lock.
```
# simplified stack samples (top 3)
1) kv_cache::pin_pages -> batch_merge::acquire_slots -> rpc_send
2) exec::generate_step -> kv_cache::get_fragment -> kv_cache::promote
3) scheduler::wait_on_batch -> batch_merge::head_of_line_wait
```
lee: also noticed kernel selection didn't change; problem looks orthogonal to ops but worse when batching heuristics keep merging very long sequences into single head-blocking batches.
maria: can you repro with a deterministic script? I can run on a mid-sized GPU.
sam: repro script (python) -- spawns 20 concurrent chats with length=32k each and continuous batching enabled:
```
# minimal repro snippet
from redwood import Client
c = Client(token=...)
def long_chat():
    resp = c.generate(model='rw-13b', input='\n'.join(['token']*32000), stream=False)
for _ in range(20):
    spawn(long_chat)
```
Works locally for me.
jonathan: quick idea: change batch-splitting so we don't merge across requests that would pin >X pages combined. i.e. add a merge heuristic: if merged_estimated_pages > merge_threshold, keep as separate batches. Could be a quick mitigation.
lee: tried that - adding a max-merged-pages of 4096 reduces the head-of-line wait and lowers rss growth in my local run. Patch diff (pseudocode):
```
- if can_merge(a,b): merge
+ if can_merge(a,b) and (a.pages + b.pages) <= MERGE_PAGES_MAX: merge
```
result: resident growth dropped from +850MB -> +90MB over 20m, p95 latency back to baseline.
perf-bot: Canary cb4d9f triggered alert: latency_slo_breach=true at 1768501228
deploy-bot: Canary cb4d9f automatically rolled back at 1768501250 due to SLO breach :warning:
maria: nice find. What's the tradeoff? do we increase overall tail for other workloads?
lee: tradeoff is slightly less batching efficiency for mixed short/long workloads. We measured token/sec drop ~3% for short-only traffic in synthetic test. But for long-context chat this avoids catastrophic fragmentation.
jonathan: long-term solution: we should add fragment coalescing and a periodic compaction pass to reduce small-fragment overhead, and make batching heuristics fragmentation-aware. Also track per-batch estimated-kv-footprint in scheduler.
sam: agree. For now we'll push the merge_pages_threshold as a canary hotfix and add a regression test in eng-runtime perf harness to catch this class of growth. I'll open PR and tag @lee @maria for review.
maria: please add a perf eval tied to the long-context prompt set so we don't regress again. Also add a metric: kv_fragments_per_1k_pages.
lee: adding that metric now. I also have a flamegraph + heaptrace in the bug ticket.
sam: thanks all. deploying hotfix to canary in ~30m, will report back. :thumbsup:
